quickAnswer: Millis has the 16th-highest share of homes in multi-unit buildings among the 50 towns we serve, 24.9% (ACS 2022) against 16.1% for the middle town. Electricity heats 15.2% of homes, and the heat pump rebate route turns on who supplies your address.
body: ## One in four homes shares a building

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 3,357 housing units in Millis, and 837 of them (24.9%) are in buildings with more than one unit. That ranks 16th of the 50 MetroWest towns we serve, ahead of the middle town's 16.1%. Buildings of three or four units hold 360 homes (10.7%), buildings of five or more hold 372 (11.1%), and two-unit buildings hold 105 (3.1%). Single-family detached houses are 2,167 units (64.6%), 34th of 50, and townhouse-style homes add 353 (10.5%).
For heating and cooling, a multi-unit building can raise questions about who owns the equipment, where outdoor units may go and how a repair affects neighbors. Renters occupy 545 households (17.2%).
## Oil, gas and a high electric share

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,284 of 3,172 occupied homes (40.5%), utility gas heats 1,164 (36.7%), and electricity heats 482 (15.2%), the 13th-highest share of the 50 towns against 10.1% for the middle town. Bottled or tank gas heats 197 (6.2%). Thirty homes list solar.
Where a home relies on electric resistance, a heat pump can often supply the same heat from less electricity. For an oil home, the question is whether to stay with delivery or change over.
## Brick, rail and Route 109

Millis was first settled in 1657 and incorporated on February 24, 1885, after it split from Medway. The Wikipedia history says clay from the pits around Causeway Street was made into bricks that built many large estates and buildings in the area and beyond, and that remnants of the pits now look like small ponds. The town's railroad, built up by Lansing Millis, helped tie it to Dedham and Boston, and the Hartford and Dedham Turnpike, today's Route 109, was built in 1806 and accepted by the town in 1896.

Industry left its mark too. Clicquot Club, which distributed the first brand of ginger ale in the United States, gave its name to the village of Clicquot, and the Herman Shoe Company factory was demolished in March 2020. Richardson's Tavern, built c. 1720, hosted George Washington for lunch in 1775. State routes 109 and 115 both run through Millis. The town is approximately 19 miles southwest of downtown Boston and is bordered by Norfolk, Sherborn, Holliston, Medfield and Medway. Clicquot Club, the ginger ale maker, was also the first company in the nation to can drinks, and today the prominent employers listed are Tresca Brothers Sand & Gravel and Roche Bros. Supermarket.
## Rivers, a swamp and older buildings

Millis covers 12.3 square miles, almost all of it land, and the Charles River and Bogastow Brook run through it. The Great Black Swamp covers hundreds of acres and divides the town from Medway. Basement humidity is worth asking about in any house. Of the town's homes, 429 (12.8%) were built in 1939 or earlier and 1,909 (56.9%) before 1980. The median home dates to 1977, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $504,100. Vacancy is 5.5% (185 units), 12th-highest of the 50 towns.
## Rebates depend on the address

We do not name an electric utility for Millis. Which rebate program a household can use is decided by whoever supplies that address, and the first step is to read the electric bill. The [heat pump page](/cities/millis/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) shows how to use the answer.

faq.q: Which heat pump rebate applies in Millis?
faq.a: That depends on the utility serving your address, and we do not name one for the town. Read your electric bill for the supplier, then ask that supplier which program covers your fuel. Do this before you sign a contract, because the answer changes which route to take.

faq.q: How many Millis households rent, and does it change who decides on heating?
faq.a: Renters occupy 545 households (17.2%), which is 25th of the 50 towns and just above the middle town's 16.4%. Owners hold 2,627 (82.8%). In a rental, a landlord or association often decides on the boiler, and a building of several units may share one system between households.

faq.q: Is electric heat common in Millis?
faq.a: More than in most towns we serve. Electricity heats 482 occupied homes, which is 15.2%, and the town ranks 13th of 50 on that measure. For those homes a heat pump is a natural option, since it delivers heat from less electricity.

faq.q: More than half of Millis homes predate 1980. Does that change the quote?
faq.a: It can. With 1,909 homes (56.9%) built before 1980, insulation, windows and ductwork differ widely from one address to the next, so a replacement unit is better sized from the house than from the old nameplate. That is why we assess the heating load of the home before quoting.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,284 Millis homes, utility gas 1,164 and bottled gas 197, with electricity at 482 as a real third. A failed system leads to a different choice at each address, and gas work needs a permit.
body: ## Four fuels, no single default

Oil leads at 40.5%, utility gas follows at 36.7% (30th of the 50 towns), and bottled gas serves 6.2%, 15th highest. No fuel dominates, which means the right answer for a dead boiler is rarely the same on two streets. Some addresses can convert to gas, some stay with oil, and some are candidates for a heat pump.
### Boilers in shared buildings

Buildings of three or four units hold 360 homes in Millis and buildings of five or more hold 372. In a building like that, one boiler can serve several households, so replacement has to be scheduled around when people can be without heat, and an association or owner has to approve. Older buildings with hot-water or steam piping need a careful pressure test after the new unit goes in.
### Questions that shape the job
- Which fuel runs the system, and how old is the unit?
- Does a gas main pass the street?
- Radiators, baseboard or ducts?
- Who owns the equipment: the occupant, a landlord or an association?
### The permit for gas equipment

In this state the person who pulls a gas permit must be a licensed plumber or gas fitter, never the homeowner. A new gas furnace or boiler then normally gets a final inspection, and the building department is the office that confirms how it works in Millis. Ask your installer who files it.
### Houses from 1960 to 1979

The 958 units built from 1960 to 1979 (28.5%) are the second-largest age group in town. Their size, the number of floors and the condition of the walls decide the heating load, and that load, not the old unit's rating, is what we use for a quote.
### If the heat fails

Call (508) 786-8755. We take emergency calls 24 hours a day, and the written estimate comes before any work starts. Heat that fails in a three- or four-unit building is urgent for every household in it.

faq.q: Is a gas conversion worth it for a Millis oil boiler?
faq.a: Only when a main reaches the house and the connection work is reasonable. Utility gas heats 36.7% of Millis homes, so check your own address. Some households do better with a new oil boiler, others with a heat pump, so compare all three in the estimate.

faq.q: Who arranges a boiler replacement in a condo building?
faq.a: It depends on whether the boiler is shared or serves one unit. A shared boiler is usually handled through the association, while a single-unit system is the owner's job, though the association may have rules. With 837 units in multi-unit buildings, ask before the work is scheduled.

faq.q: What does a propane furnace swap involve?
faq.a: Bottled gas heats 197 Millis homes, and the fuel is delivered to a tank rather than piped in. Replacing the furnace means checking the tank, the lines and the flue as well as the unit itself, and a licensed gas fitter has to pull the permit for the new equipment.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Millis has 2,167 detached houses, 353 townhouse-style homes and 837 units in multi-unit buildings, and each type cools differently. Ducts suit some houses, and ductless mini-splits suit homes without them and apartments.
body: ## Cooling four kinds of Millis home

Detached houses are 64.6% of the 3,357 units, 34th of the 50 towns, so Millis leans less on single-family houses than most of the towns we serve. Townhouse-style units add 10.5%. Buildings of three or four units hold 10.7% of housing, buildings of five or more 11.1% and two-unit buildings 3.1%. The Census counts no mobile homes in town.
### Detached and attached

A detached house can often take central air if its ducts are in good shape, and it usually has a side or back yard for the condenser. A townhouse-style home shares walls and may have less room outside, so the outdoor unit location becomes the first question to settle. The town covers 12.2 square miles of land, and housing runs from houses with a yard to apartments with none, so each address needs its own answer on where the condenser or line set can go.
### Apartments and condos

If tenants pay their own electric bills, giving each apartment its own ductless system lets each household run its own cooling. Condo associations may restrict where outdoor units go and how line sets run along the exterior.
### Homes without ducts

Median build year is 1977, and many older homes were built before central air was common. Of the 3,357 units, 1,909 (56.9%) predate 1980. A ductless mini-split cools one room or zone with a small indoor head, no ductwork and only a small hole through the wall.
### What shapes a cooling plan
- The rooms that run hot, such as top-floor bedrooms.
- Panel capacity for another circuit.
- Where an outdoor unit can sit.
- Whether one heat pump could handle heating as well.
### Electric heat and summer

Electricity heats 15.2% of Millis homes, so many households already depend on the electric bill in January. For them one heat pump can cover both seasons. The [heat pump page](/cities/millis/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the program route.

faq.q: Can a Millis condo owner install a mini-split?
faq.a: Often, but the association may have rules for outdoor units and line sets. Ask the association first, then confirm where the condenser can sit. Because 24.9% of Millis units are in multi-unit buildings, many owners face this question, and the answer varies from one building to the next.

faq.q: Is one big unit better than several small ones?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A single large system can be oversized for rooms that rarely need cooling, and an oversized unit shuts off before it removes moisture. Several smaller heads let each room run on its own. The layout of the house decides, and we size from the house.

faq.q: Can I cool a townhouse-style home with a mini-split?
faq.a: Usually. Attached homes are 10.5% of Millis housing, and they often have little outdoor space, which suits a compact condenser and a short line set. The home's walls and any association rules decide where the equipment can go, so check those before ordering.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Which program pays for a Millis heat pump depends on the utility serving your address, which we do not name. Electricity already heats 482 homes (15.2%), and oil heats 1,284, so the first step is to read your bill.
body: ## Start with the electric bill

Rebates run through whichever utility supplies the address, so find out who sends your electric bill and what it offers for your fuel. If Mass Save is the route, the 2026 whole-home figure is $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500. Full terms are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Which households gain most

Oil heats 1,284 homes and bottled gas 197, and both fuels arrive by delivery, which a heat pump can replace. Electricity heats 482 homes (15.2%), which ranks 13th, compared with the middle town's 10.1%. Where that is resistance heat, a heat pump delivers more heat per unit of electricity. The Census also lists 30 homes with solar.
### Age against the 2000 cutoff

Only 435 units (13.0%) date from 2000 or later, and just 285 (8.5%) from 2010 on. At the other end, 1,909 units (56.9%) predate 1980. Most Millis houses therefore reach a heat pump through an assessment or past work rather than the build date, and the assessment also shows where air sealing would lower the load.
### Multi-unit buildings

With 837 units in multi-unit buildings, a ductless system can heat and cool one apartment without touching the rest of the building. Where a building is shared, ask the owner or association first. Our [cooling page](/cities/millis/air-conditioning-installation-repair) shows how ductless suits shared buildings.
### Houses with ducts and without

Detached houses (2,167) with ductwork can use a ducted unit. Others suit ductless heads in the rooms that matter. Many houses use a mix, and we assess the heating load before quoting. Of the 3,357 units, 2,167 are detached, 353 townhouse-style and 837 in multi-unit buildings, so ducted, ductless and multi-zone setups all have a place, and the building type is usually what points to one of them first.

faq.q: How do I find out which program applies to my Millis home?
faq.a: Look at your electric bill to see who the utility is, then ask that utility whether it is a Mass Save sponsor and what it offers for your fuel. Call before you sign a contract, since the answer decides which program you apply to.

faq.q: Can I use a heat pump alongside my existing furnace?
faq.a: Yes. A furnace can stay as a backup for the coldest days while the heat pump does the rest of the work. This partial setup suits many Millis houses on oil or tank gas, and the existing ductwork and heating load decide whether it makes sense for yours.

faq.q: Do heat pumps work in a Massachusetts winter?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are built for it. Installation quality and sizing matter more than brand, which is why we assess the heating load before we quote. A house in the 1,909-unit group built before 1980 may also need air sealing to get the most from a heat pump.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Millis splits between oil, gas and electric heat, and each needs a different visit. With 545 renter households and 837 units in multi-unit buildings, a tune-up often involves a landlord or association as well.
body: ## A visit that matches the fuel

Oil leads Millis heating, utility gas follows, electricity comes third and bottled gas trails. Oil: burner and heat exchanger cleaning, filter and nozzle changes, a combustion test. Gas: burner, venting and safety controls. Electric and heat pumps: filters, coils and refrigerant-side checks.
### Rental and shared buildings

Renters occupy 545 households (17.2%) and owners 2,627 (82.8%). A boiler that quits in a three-family or larger building leaves several households cold, and in the heating season state rules set minimums of 68 F by day and 64 F overnight for rentals, with the landlord usually paying for heat. A planned visit before October is easier than a night emergency. This is general information, not legal advice.
### Systems in a 1977 town

The same applies to the 958 units from 1960 to 1979 (28.5%). Oil burners from those years may still be running, and a combustion test shows whether one is still worth cleaning or has reached the point where a heat pump or new boiler is the better plan.

The median Millis home dates to 1977, and the 1,013 units (30.2%) built from 1980 to 1999 are the largest age band. Equipment in houses of those years has had time to wear, so a tune-up is the moment to ask how many seasons remain and to plan a replacement rather than react.
### Vacant units

The Census counts 185 vacant units (5.5%), 12th highest of the 50 towns. A unit that stays empty over winter still has a boiler or furnace, and a visit before the cold arrives helps avoid a surprise at move-in.
### Calendar
- Late summer or early fall: heating.
- Spring: cooling.
- Any time: noise, smell, soot, short cycling or an unusual bill.
### What to have ready

Have the fuel, the system's rough age, the nameplate details and a note of what you noticed ready when you call; the technician can then arrive with the right parts and questions. For a shared building, add who owns the equipment and who can approve the visit.
Should a visit point to replacement, the [heating page](/cities/millis/heating-installation-repair) takes it from there.

faq.q: How often should an oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season. Oil heats 40.5% of Millis homes, so many households need this visit. Skipping it can let soot build up, which may lower efficiency and lead to breakdowns when the weather is coldest.

faq.q: Should a landlord schedule a tune-up before winter?
faq.a: It is a good habit. A failure leaves every tenant cold at once, and the state sets minimum indoor temperatures for rentals during the heating season. In Millis, 545 households rent. With 17.2% of Millis households renting, a planned fall visit beats a cold-night call.

faq.q: Do heat pumps and electric systems need a visit?
faq.a: Yes, though it is lighter than for combustion equipment. Electricity heats 15.2% of Millis homes, and those systems need clean filters and coils, a clear condensate drain and a technician reading the refrigerant side. Keep outdoor units clear of snow and leaves.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Millis has 429 units built in 1939 or earlier, 285 built since 2010 and a quarter of its housing in shared buildings. Leaky old buildings and tight new ones have different air problems, and shared buildings add their own.
body: ## Air in houses and in shared buildings

The 2022 ACS puts 429 units (12.8%) in the 1939-or-earlier band and 522 (15.5%) in the 1940 to 1959 band, with 285 (8.5%) built since 2010. A quarter of the town's units sit in multi-unit buildings. The air issues differ between a detached house and a shared building.
### Older houses
Millis has 1,909 units from before 1980 (56.9%), so the older-house profile covers more than half the town.

Gaps in older buildings let some pollutants out and pull dust, pollen and basement air in. Ductwork of that age may have collected dust for decades. If a renovation is on the list, ask a qualified specialist to test for older materials first.
### Newer, tighter houses

Tighter construction keeps energy in and also keeps moisture, cooking fumes and furnishing chemicals inside unless ventilation keeps up. A bathroom fan that runs and a range hood that vents outside help.
### Apartments and condos

In multi-unit buildings, air can travel between units through shared walls, halls and sometimes shared ducts. Sealing gaps, keeping a bathroom fan working and changing filters help. Smoke, cooking odors and moisture can travel this way, and a building owner may need to look at shared ductwork.
### Water, swamp and basements

Charles River, brook and swamp are part of the town's geography, and the Wikipedia history says the town has many areas of town-administered land. Indoors, the useful number is the humidity reading in the basement, which a basic meter shows, and it should stay in a comfortable range through both seasons.

The Charles River and Bogastow Brook run through Millis, the Great Black Swamp covers hundreds of acres, and water makes up 0.90% of the town's area. Clay pits on Causeway Street left small ponds. Basement dampness can have many sources, so find the source before buying a dehumidifier.
### What we can help with
- Better filtration.
- Humidity control.
- Ventilation for tight homes.
- Cleaning ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged, plus fixing the cause.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. A technician can look inside, and cleaning is justified by visible mold, heavy dirt or damage from pests or a renovation. A dusty grille alone is usually a filter issue, so check the filter first before paying for a cleaning.

Yes, through gaps, shared walls or shared ducts. With 837 units in multi-unit buildings, Millis has plenty of homes where this happens. Sealing gaps and running bathroom and kitchen fans helps, and a building owner may need to look at the shared ductwork.

faq.q: Is a damp basement a heating-system problem?
faq.a: Usually not. Moisture can rise from soil, leak from a pipe or condense where humid air meets cold masonry. A dehumidifier controls the air, but a leak or poor grading outside must be fixed at its source, so trace the cause before sizing any equipment.
